# Alpha-OSK

> A free, open-source on-screen keyboard for Windows and Linux, with word
> prediction that learns on the user's own machine. Built for people who cannot
> comfortably use a physical keyboard but can move a cursor.

Alpha-OSK is a desktop application. The user clicks keys in a floating keyboard
window and the keystrokes are delivered to whichever application currently has
operating-system focus. The keyboard never takes focus itself.

Prediction merges an n-gram model of the user's own vocabulary with a spatial
model of the keys surrounding the one actually clicked, so a mis-clicked key is
still completed to the intended word. There is no large language model and no
GPU requirement, and the model never leaves the machine.

Key facts:

- Licence: MIT. Free for personal and commercial use. No account, no subscription.
- Platforms: Windows 10/11 (EV-signed installer, auto-updating) and Linux
  (AppImage, requires xdotool on X11 or ydotool on Wayland). macOS is in
  progress and not released.
- Privacy: learning is entirely on-device. Password fields pause learning
  automatically. The one feature that transmits anything is optional voice
  dictation, which is off by default and requires the user's own Deepgram API
  key; audio is sent only while the microphone is open.
- Author: Owen Kent, a wheelchair user with muscular dystrophy who uses the
  keyboard daily to develop it.
